route: Work permit (Labor Division) and work visa

permit.applies: The employer applies to the Labor Division (Director of Labor) for a general work permit, with a statutory declaration by employer and worker; the work visa follows under the Immigration Act.
permit.first: Proof the position was advertised in local media for three consecutive weeks and that the search found no suitably qualified and available citizen (a labour-market test); a bond.

fees.what: Non-resident worker fee, paid by the employer, per worker per quarter (Non-resident Workers (Fee) Act 1987, s. 203)

permit.eligibility: evidence that the proposed applicant meets the prescribed minimum level of education and experience;
permit.validityNote: A work permit runs no longer than the worker's contract; each extension or renewal (except of a temporary work permit) is for up to five years depending on the contract (Labor (Non-Resident Workers) Act 2018, s. 111(7), as amended by P.L. 2025-43). A temporary purpose permit (emergencies, training, short-term technical work) lasts up to six months a year, extendable once.
permit.exemptNote: None for a performer: the Labor (Non-Resident Workers) Act 2018's exemptions (s. 108(2), the whole list) name none.

sources.title: Labor (Non-Resident Workers) Act 2018, 16 MIRC ch. 1 (Nitijela of the Marshall Islands, consolidated copy)
sources.said: Any employer intending to apply for a work permit for any other occupation not listed on the Occupational Shortages List may apply for a general work permit. … Any extension or renewal of any type of work permit, except for a temporary work permit, shall be valid for up to five 5 years dependent on the duration of the contract, following the expiration of the previous period granted. … proof the position has been advertised in local media for three (3) consecutive weeks; … proof that the search process was unable to yield a suitably qualified and available citizen worker; … evidence that the proposed applicant meets the prescribed minimum level of education and experience; … The Director shall, within twenty-one (21) days of the complete application being submitted, inform the employer in writing of the outcome of the application. … AN ACT to repeal the Labor (Non-Resident Workers) Act 2006 … a citizen of the United States; … Any extension or renewal of any type of work permit, except for a temporary work permit, shall be valid for up to five 5 years dependent on the duration of the contract

sources.title: Non-resident Workers (Fee) Act 1987 (as amended by P.L. 2009-23), Nitijela copy
sources.said: Every employer of a non-resident worker shall pay to the Secretary a fee of $250 per worker per quarter.

sources.title: Nitijela of the Marshall Islands, Labor (Non-Resident Workers) Act 2018 (16 MIRC ch. 1), s. 108 (the exemptions) and s. 116 (temporary purpose work permit)
sources.said: §108. Requirement to a hold work permit (1) Any person who is not a citizen of the Republic is prohibited from undertaking employment in the Republic unless that person is: (a) the holder of a work permit granted under this Chapter; or (b) exempt under this Chapter from the requirement to hold a work permit. (2) The following persons are exempt from the requirement to hold a work permit: (a) a person who is for the time being entitled to any immunity from jurisdiction by or under the Diplomatic Privileges and Immunities Act 1988; (b) ... International Organization Immunities Act 1974; (c) a citizen of the United States; (d) a citizen of the Republic Palau or the Federated States of Micronesia; provided that ... reciprocal treatment ...; (e) United States contractor personnel and their official dependents; (f) a member of the crew of any commercial aircraft ... for a period of ten (10) days ...; (g) a member of the crew of any ship fishing ...; (h) any person employed by a Government Ministry, Department or other Government Statutory entity. (i) any person covered under any international agreement ... ; ... §116. Temporary purpose work permit. (1) Any employer intending to hire a non-resident worker for a period of up to six (6) months in any calendar year to: (a) address emergencies if and when they arise; (b) train local staff; or (c) carry out short-term technical work for which suitably skilled labor is not readily available, may apply for a work permit under this section.

note: Layer 3 cited the Labor (Non-Resident Workers) Act 2006; it was repealed by the Labor (Non-Resident Workers) Act 2018 (16 MIRC ch. 1, as amended to P.L. 2025-43), read here from the Nitijela's own copy; the route and the free list (US citizens, and Palau and FSM citizens where reciprocal) are unchanged. Section 111(7) ties the permit to the contract requiring residence and allows extensions or renewals of up to five years with the contract, but its first-term wording is garbled ('not in excess of the ... contractual obligation requiring residency in the Republic in excess of one (1) year'), so no first term is modelled. The application fee is prescribed by the Minister (s. 151), amount not found. A temporary purpose permit (up to six months a year) exists for emergencies, training and short-term technical work, not performers. Read 2026-11-04 in the Act on the Nitijela's site: no exemption for performers. It names no union step or pay rule, but the Minister's regulations (s. 151) weren't found, so those stay unknown. Re-read 2026-11-04: rmiparliament.org's copy (1987-0006_1.pdf) answered with an error page; the fact stands on its reading of 2026-11-01.
